turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. 

I made the appointment because, well, I keep losing chunks of time during the day. I find myself constantly re-reading emails and texts, or reopening folders on my computer over and over. And before I can even leave the house or really start my work, I end up mentally replaying conversations I've had. 

It's... it's like I'm just trying to prove to myself that I didn't make some serious mistake somewhere. It's taking up a lot of my time and getting pretty frustrating, so I figured I should come in.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient describes a persistent, intrusive doubt about having made a serious mistake, which drives their repetitive behaviors.
symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient explicitly reports engaging in repetitive behaviors (re-reading emails, reopening folders) and mental acts (replaying conversations) to alleviate their doubt.

turns.doctor_question: When you are re-reading those emails or reopening those folders, do you feel an intense, internal urge or pressure to do so to prevent something bad from happening, or to stop a specific distressing thought?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, exactly. Like I was saying, it really comes down to trying to prove to myself that I didn't make some serious mistake. It is a really intense pressure. 

If I don't go back and re-read those emails, or reopen the folders to check what I did, I just can't shake the thought that I messed up something critical. So I feel like I have to keep doing it—or keep mentally replaying those conversations—just to relieve that feeling and convince myself everything is okay. If I don't give in and check, the feeling just builds up and I can't actually move on and start my work.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient describes an intrusive, persistent thought of having made a serious mistake that they 'can't shake' and that builds up if not addressed.
symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient confirms feeling an intense pressure to perform repetitive behaviors (re-reading emails, reopening folders, mentally replaying conversations) to relieve the distressing thought of having made a mistake.
